newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand says no more troubled finance firms.
newsitem.headline: Thailand says no more troubled finance firms.

text.p: The Bank of Thailand on Monday said there would be no announcements of more new troubled finance firms in the country after it identified 16 ailing ones last week and forced them to merge with healthy ones.
It also assured depositors of the 16 affected firms that they need not worry about their deposits and asked them not to panic.
The central bank also ordered all finance firms in the country to cap their deposit rates for promissory notes at 14 percent and their call rates at 11 percent.

Central bank governor Rerngchai Marakanond told a news conference that the authorities would do their best to help foreign creditors of troubled finance companies recover their funds. But he did not give details on how the help would be implemented.
"I would like to ask depositors to understand and not be panicked as they will be fully protected..and there (are) no 17 or 18 troubled finance companies as rumoured," he said.
On the limit placed on interest rates offered by finance firms, he said: "This limit will help reduce the interest rate burden in the sector."
Thailand's troubled finance sector has been hard hit by overexposure to the depressed property sector and business has been affected by the country's worst economic slump in over a decade.
